  "codebook": {
    "definition": "'Credit-claiming' is defined as a statement in which a legislator asserts personal or collective responsibility for successfully securing a specific, tangible government action, benefit, grant, or legislative outcome for their constituents or the nation.",
    "clarification": "This includes announcing the award of federal grants or resources to local entities, securing specific earmarks or federal funding, explicitly mentioning the passage of a sponsored bill or amendment, successfully influencing an agency decision (bureaucratic casework with concrete results), or obtaining a facility/project for the district. The text must explicitly state or strongly imply that the senator's actions (e.g., authoring the provision, requesting the funds, writing a letter, brokering an agreement) were instrumental in achieving the tangible outcome.         "text": "U S Senator Charles E Schumer today announced that Westchester County has received two federal grants totaling 134,004...         "text": "SENATE ADOPTS NELSON AMENDMENT TO PROVIDE FAIRNESS FOR U S CATTLE PRODUCERS... Nebraska s Senator Ben Nelson today said he was gratified that his amendment to prevent the USDA from allowing some Japanese beef imports... passed on a bipartisan vote of 72 to 26.",

      },

        "text": "Administrator finally responds to Sen Landrieu s letter in testimony... Dr McClellan said the more than 250 000 Louisiana seniors... will now have until December 31 2006 to file without penalty... I am pleased that the agency has finally come to its senses and recognized the inconsistency our delegation brought to its attention last month.",

      }
    ],
    "negative_clarification": "Texts should NOT be classified as credit-claiming if they merely involve 'position taking' (expressing support or opposition for a policy without claiming a concrete achievement), announcing the mere introduction or co-sponsorship of a bill (without indicating it has passed or reached a major milestone like committee passage), criticizing political opponents or agencies, giving broad policy speeches, holding hearings, or announcing routine town hall meetings ('advertising').",
    "negative_examples": [
      {
        "text": "Senate Majority Leader Sen. Harry Reid released the following statement today in response to President Bush's call for a global greenhouse-gases emissions goal: The Bush Administration's 'head in the sand' position on global warming has defied reason and common sense.",
        "explanation": "This text exemplifies position taking and blame-generating. The senator is criticizing an opponent's policy without claiming credit for any personal, tangible achievements or securing particularized benefits."
      },

        "text": "Today Senator Edward M Kennedy introduced legislation to enhance stem cell research and to strengthen anti cloning provisions... The misguided fears of today can t be allowed to deny the cures of tomorrow...",

      },

        "explanation": "This is a form of advertising. The senator is announcing their availability to constituents rather than taking credit for a specific government action, grant, or legislative achievement."
      }
    ]
  }
